season: All year, once a month per side (the nth weekday of the month). A City holiday cancels that day's sweep; the City says the streets are swept "on their next regularly scheduled day", which is the next month's. No make-up day.

hours.source: Not in the City's schedule, which says only AM or PM. Read on posted signs in Google Street View: "NO PARKING 9 AM TO 12 NOON, 1ST TUESDAY EACH MONTH, STREET SWEEPING" (Ward St, 1600 block, south side, imagery Jan 2015) and "NO PARKING 12:30 PM TO 3:30 PM, 1ST WEDNESDAY EACH MONTH" (Acton St, 1600 block, east side, imagery Mar 2025); both match the schedule's day for that side. To confirm with the City that every AM and PM sign reads the same.

placement.method: A row goes on each segment of its street (its type if the row names one, else the street's main types) whose numbers on the row's side are at least 50% inside the row's range, on the side holding the row's parity (N and E odd, S and W even, as the PDFs say). A segment's odd side is the address points' (4 points, 80%) where they decide, else the centerline's ranges; when only the ranges say it and the row's word points clearly the other way (conf >= 0.7), the word wins ("compass over ranges"); with no odd side, or numbers that are not the segment's at all, the side facing the row's word. A row whose numbers place nothing is walked along its street between its two cross streets ("Terminus", "Cul De Sac" = a dead end inside the City, "City Limit" = one at the City boundary). A side two rows give different days keeps the row whose numbers and cross streets both put it there, then the row with the narrower range; still tied, both rules stay.

optOut.note: Blocks named in the schedule's Opt-Out column left the program (Resolution 54,513-N.S., 1987) and are not swept. A segment whose numbers lie wholly inside opted-out hundred blocks of its street (any row of the street naming them) is left off, both sides. status = the City layer's own status for it.

cityStatusLayer.note: The Street Sweep Status layer's own status for the segments the schedule placed. Not used to place rules; the schedule wins.
